meaning: Which test the value was judged in: random (papers drawn at random; 147 in the judging behind the final verdict) or locked (83 held-out papers).
PubMed identifier of the paper the value comes from.
Which reading stored the value: CatLog, or plain (one plain reading of each paper by Claude Opus 5.5).
Identifier of the value in the judging’s records (each judged value is a ‘claim’), for tracing its verdict.
The constant the reading stored the value as: kcat, Km or kcat/Km.
The number as the reading stored it and the judges saw it, in the unit of the Unit column.
Unit of the stored value: s⁻¹ for kcat, mM for Km, mM⁻¹ s⁻¹ for kcat/Km.
The printed cell and unit, as the reading recorded them.
Enzyme name as the reading stored it.
Organism the enzyme comes from, as the reading stored it.
Wild type, mutant or construct, as the reading stored it.
The substrate the constant refers to, as the reading stored it.
Other substrates, cofactors or electron acceptors in the assay, as the reading stored them; blank = not stated.
Assay pH as the reading stored it; blank = not stated.
Assay temperature in °C as the reading stored it; blank = not stated.
Table, figure or text section holding the value, shortened from the reading’s own location.
The paper’s label or footnote for the value, as the reading’s notes quote or name it (‘the reading's details:’ marks a paraphrase); else blank.
The final verdict: the one two judges agreed on; where the first two split, a third judge’s vote decided. Codes in the notes.
Each judge’s verdict: j1 and j2 are the first two judges; j3, a third judge, was called where they split.
Word for word, the reasons of the judges whose verdict became final, each marked j1, j2 or j3.
For the 11 split values, the outvoted judge’s verdict and reason; blank where the judges agreed.
Where the first judge found the value in the paper: page, table row and column, or text passage.
Disputed: only this reading stored the value (96 values). Agreeing pair: matched by number with the other reading’s value, sampled for judging (1 value).
Random test only: verdict and votes in that test’s first judging, before the judging that gave the final verdict; blank for the locked test.
CatLog’s 40 values only: the printed header or sentence giving the value’s unit; for 7334001, both readings of the contested exponent.
CatLog’s 40 values only: the printed cell with its printed unit taken at face value, converted to the stored unit; both readings for 7334001.
CatLog’s 34 deliberate unit changes: printed cell to stored value, then the paper’s own numbers on the scale; 9973343’s per-row figures computed for this table.
Agents’ checks against the paper made after the judging (post hoc), or a note that none has run; blank for the random test’s plain-reading values.
The reading’s own notes on the value (place, assay, caveats), in full, as the judges saw them.
